questions.q: What is the first step in this lesson's four-layer JSON pipeline?
options: Land the JSON raw into a table with a single VARIANT column, untouched
Immediately write the final reporting query against the raw JSON file
Convert the JSON to CSV before loading it
Delete any nested fields before loading
questions.explain: The pipeline always starts by landing the JSON raw in a VARIANT column, with no reshaping yet.

questions.q: In the pipeline's final reporting query shown in this lesson, why is there no VARIANT syntax, colon notation, or FLATTEN visible?
options: Because all of that was already resolved one layer earlier, inside the views built over the raw JSON
Because Snowflake automatically strips VARIANT columns from final queries
Because the reporting query doesn't actually use any of the JSON data
Because FLATTEN can only be used once per database
questions.explain: The views handle colon notation and FLATTEN once; the final reporting query is a plain JOIN over already-typed columns from those views.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is one advantage of layering (raw table → view → reporting query) instead of writing one giant query?
options: Each stage can be verified independently instead of debugging one very long query all at once
Layering makes the JSON load slower on purpose for safety
It's required because Snowflake cannot run queries longer than 10 lines
It removes the need to ever check row counts
questions.explain: Layering lets you confirm the raw load, then the view's output, then the final report, one at a time — rather than debugging one large query.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe the relationship between this JSON pipeline and the staging → warehouse → reporting layering from Lesson 30?
options: It's the same layering discipline, just applied to JSON instead of CSV/relational sources
They are unrelated concepts that happen to share similar names
JSON pipelines should skip staging entirely, unlike Lesson 30's approach
Lesson 30's layering only applies to Snowpipe, never to VARIANT data
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly ties this pipeline's layering to the same staging → warehouse → reporting discipline taught in Lesson 30, just for semi-structured data.

questions.q: What makes a query result 'report-shaped,' as this lesson uses the term?
options: It has plain, typed columns — no VARIANT visible — ready for a BI tool or a business question
It must contain at least one VARIANT column
It can only have exactly one column
It must be sorted alphabetically by every column
questions.explain: Report-shaped means the VARIANT/JSON complexity has already been resolved upstream, leaving plain typed columns a BI tool can use directly.
